clue.text: Reproduce broadcast operation

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the whole word is the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is told to repeat a radio or television operation for another airing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduce broadcast' looks like an instruction about a programme, but REPRODUCE rearranged gives PROCEDURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical operation is called a procedure in medical language.

clue.text: Indicate the stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to show with a finger
second meaning: a particular moment in a process

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like pointing out the theatre stage; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to direct attention; as a noun it means a moment or juncture, as in 'at this point'.

clue.text: Musical entertainment: Laurence to conduct

parts.note: a staged work set to music
the initials of T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A man named Laurence is invited to conduct a musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence stands for T. E. Lawrence, whose initials give the last two letters, although his surname is usually spelt with a w.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a business or machine is to run it, which is to operate it.

clue.text: Instruct to improve journalist in future years, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each of those words counts

parts.note: initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A trainee journalist is told to work on getting better over the coming years.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to teach someone in a morally or intellectually uplifting way.

clue.text: Untidy punk met criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: A scruffy punk encounters a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or clothes are uncombed and messy, a close synonym.

clue.text: First flier gets the breakfast?

parts.note: surface reading: a pioneer aviator, the first person to fly
setter's reading: the bird up at dawn that catches the worm, as the proverb says

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the first riser among birds catches the worm; a person who gets up very early earns the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names someone who rises or arrives very early, taken from the proverb about the worm.

clue.text: Firstly, settle in good home and express relief

indicators.note: firstly points to taking just the opening letter of the next two words

parts.note: abbreviation, as on maps and sports tables

explanation.surface: Someone moves into a nice house and lets out a breath of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigh is a long audible breath, often given when a worry passes.

clue.text: Will Robin's man become bright red?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Will ..., one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws
second meaning: a vivid red colour

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Robin's companion will blush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense, but it is the first name of Will Scarlet, a Merry Man in the Robin Hood legends.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is also the name of a brilliant red hue, as in scarlet fever.

clue.text: Go everywhere — run after the ball

indicators.note: after places the word before it at the end, behind the word that follows

parts.note: a globe is a ball or sphere
to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: A footballer is urged to chase the ball all over the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel widely, visiting many countries around the world.

clue.text: Poem from Irish city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a humorous five-line verse
second meaning: a city on the River Shannon

explanation.surface: A poem has come from a city in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic five-line verse form shares its name with a city in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Concerning one boy's motive

explanation.surface: Something about a particular boy explains why things happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motive is the reason behind an action, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Finally my tea's different, it's sexy!

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone at last finds their tea has changed, and declares it sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' tempts you to take a last letter, but the six letters of the next two words already make the answer; it is only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes erotic or passionate scenes, a synonym for sexy.

clue.text: Short-lived things for which I'm safely treated

indicators.note: to be treated is to be processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone says that, thanks to a treatment, they have come through safely despite something fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult mayflies are insects that famously live only a day or so.

clue.text: Wind something that's child's play

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a very easy task

explanation.surface: A gentle wind is so easy that a child could manage it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a gentle wind and informal for an effortless task, as in 'the exam was a doddle'.

clue.text: Spoil lousy arrangement to a seriously damaging degree

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so the letters of the word before are reordered

explanation.surface: A poor arrangement is spoilt in a way that causes real harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinously means in a way that causes ruin, an adverb of serious harm.

clue.text: Forceful queen involved in genetic development

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the other
development turns something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful queen takes part in advances in genetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means vigorous and full of force, a close synonym of forceful.

clue.text: Fiddlers' corkscrews

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cheats or swindlers, as in fiddling the accounts
second meaning: things that spiral or turn

explanation.walkthrough: Fiddlers look like violinists, but here they are people who fiddle, or cheat; the possessive merely joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a swindler, and also anything that twists, such as a spiralling corkscrew.

clue.text: Worried, insisted on order

indicators.note: worried means harried or shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An anxious person demanded neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is the state of being neat, which is what order means here.

clue.text: Accustomed to judge interfering, but hurt

indicators.note: something interfering gets in the middle of things, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: inured means hardened or used to something

explanation.surface: Someone used to a meddling judge is nonetheless hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Injured means harmed or wounded, a synonym of hurt as an adjective.

clue.text: Wise king alone with Scottish man

explanation.surface: A wise monarch is alone except for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king of Israel is proverbial for his wisdom.

clue.text: Take away, when allowed in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England

explanation.surface: Something may be removed whenever that is permitted on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to remove or strike out, so it means to take away.

clue.text: Uncoil naughty black young feline

indicators.note: a naughty thing misbehaves, so the letters will not keep their order

parts.note: abbreviation used for black in pencil grades

explanation.surface: A mischievous black kitten is told to stretch out of its curl.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion cub is a baby lion, and lions are big cats, so it is a young feline.

clue.text: Married prisoner goes to jail with Capone

explanation.surface: A wed convict is sent to prison alongside the gangster Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjugal means relating to marriage, as in conjugal rights.

clue.text: Runs in to dry gardening tool

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the following one

parts.note: to towel is to rub dry

explanation.surface: Someone dashes inside to dry off a garden implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for digging in the garden.

clue.text: Principle rule

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a rule of principle; the two words each separately give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a doctrine held as true, a principle or rule of belief.

clue.text: Strange eagle's nest, so-called

indicators.note: so-called means as it is called, pointing to how a word is said rather than written

parts.note: an eyrie is an eagle's nest

explanation.surface: An eagle's nest is said to be an odd place.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, close to strange.

clue.text: Oriental trips (by arrangement) undertaken with brio

indicators.note: something done by arrangement is set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Journeys to the East are made with great enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit and spirit, a French borrowing close to vivacity.

clue.text: Handy treatment for groom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cosmetic treatment of the hands and nails
second meaning: to tidy the nails

explanation.surface: A bridegroom is offered a useful beauty treatment before the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' seems to mean useful, but it is literal: a treatment for the hands. 'Groom' seems to be the bridegroom, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a beauty treatment for the hands and fingernails; the verb means to trim and tidy them.

clue.text: Said to have declined and changed colour

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the wanted word is one that is pronounced like another

parts.note: declined in the sense of passed away

explanation.surface: Something reportedly faded and turned a different shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed means coloured with a dye, so its hue has been altered.

clue.text: Bobby, the artist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British police officer, nicknamed a bobby
second meaning: John ..., English landscape painter

explanation.walkthrough: Bobby looks like a first name, but it is British slang for a police officer; the painter is John Constable of The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest rank of police officer, and John Constable was a celebrated English painter.
